sources.entry: Gitit - Wiki program that stores pages and uploaded files in a git repository, which can then be modified using the VCS command line tools or the wiki's web interface. GPL-2.0 Haskell

summary.one_liner: Gitit is a Haskell wiki program that stores pages and uploaded files in a git (or darcs/mercurial) repository, editable from the command line or the web interface.
summary.what_it_does: Gitit runs a wiki web server built on Happstack, using pandoc for markup processing. Pages and uploaded files live in a git repository by default, and can also be stored in darcs or mercurial repositories, so they can be edited with the VCS command-line tools or through the web interface. Pandoc markdown is the default markup, with reStructuredText, LaTeX, HTML, DocBook and Emacs Org-mode also supported. Features named in the README include categories, TeX math (MathJax, MathML or raw), syntax highlighting of source code, optional page caching, site-wide and per-page Atom feeds, and Haskell plugins. Gitit can also be embedded as a library in another Happstack application.
use_cases: Run a self-hosted wiki backed by git
Edit wiki pages with a text editor and git commits
Publish markdown or reStructuredText documentation as a website
Host a wiki with math and syntax-highlighted code
Add a wiki to an existing Haskell Happstack application
Serve a wiki behind Apache or nginx reverse proxy
notable: Wiki content is plain files in a git repository, so pages can be cloned, edited and pushed with normal git tools
Supports git, darcs and mercurial as the storage backend via configuration
Page metadata block sets format, categories, table of contents and title
Optional caching with a cache-expiry endpoint and an expireGititCache helper for VCS hooks
Can be used as a library inside a Happstack application
caveats: Installation requires the Haskell toolchain (stack or cabal); the README recommends stack
Caching is off by default, and cached pages are not refreshed when edited directly through git or darcs
Plugin support adds to binary size and memory use and can be disabled at compile time
